1 3-The brief facts of the case which are required to be stated are that on the application under Section 156(3) Cr.PC. of the revisionist, a first information report was lodged on 21.02.2022 under Section 419, 420, 406, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)(v)(a) SC/ST Act against Chandra Shekhar Chaubey,
Paramhans Chaubey, Ghanshyam Upadhyay and Shyambabu Upadhyay, in which after culmination of investigation, charge-sheet dated 17.04.2022 was filed against Paramhans Chaubey, Ghanshyam Babu Upadhyay and Shyam Babu Upadhyay for the offence under Section 419, 420, 406 I.P.C.

sentences.text: At the stage of taking cognizance, opposite party no. 2 has moved an undated application under Section 190(1)(b) Cr.P.C. alleging inter-alia that the investigating officer has not written her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and with a view to extend undue favour to the accused persons written her statement in the case diary on his own and as such, investigating officer did not conduct fair investigation and deliberately did not submit charge-sheet under Sections 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)(va) of SC/ST Act against the accused persons which has been rejected by the impugned order dated 23.05.2023.

4-The main substratum of argument of learned counsel for the revisionist is that the investigating officer, without recording the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. of the complainant, wrote her statement in the case diary on his own.

The accused persons using caste derogatory words had extended threat of life to the complainant but the said averment has not been mentioned by the investigating officer while writing the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. of the complainant

,
therefore, learned Magistrate has committed legal error in not summoning the accused persons for the offence under Section 3(1)(2)(va) of SC/ST Act.
5-On the other hand, learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel appearing on behalf of the opposite parties vehemently opposed the submission of learned counsel for the revisionist by contending that during investigation, complainant did not make any allegation against the investigating officer whereas she was very much aware about the investigation, pursuant to her F.I.R. dated 21.02.2022.
It is also submitted that the fair investigation is not only the legal right of the complainant but also a legal right of the accused.
So far as the grievance of the complainant-revisionist is concerned, it is argued that in view of Section 216 Cr.P.C., charge can be altered at any stage of the trial.

6-Having heard the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perusing the record, I find substance in the submissions of learned A.G.A. and in view of provisions of Section 216 Cr.P.C., I do not find any good ground to interfere in the impugned order 23.05.2023 at this stage.
7-The criminal revision lacks merit, and is accordingly, rejected.

Saurabh  Bandana Devi vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123188256/
